title: Why do rivers flood?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: What causes a river to flood?
Why does a river keep rising after the rain stops?
Why do towns flood so easily?

explain.say: A river floods when more water reaches it than its channel can carry, so it spills over its banks. The graph shows how a river rises and falls after a storm, called a flood hydrograph.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a river from source to sea. Look at the source, the upper course and the tributary. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Heavy rain falls across the river's whole catchment. Some soaks into the ground, but if the soil is already soaked, frozen or covered in concrete, much more runs straight off into the river.
The river rises after a delay called lag time, while water travels over and through the land. Steep slopes, bare ground and towns shorten the lag and make a higher, sharper peak.
At the peak the river may burst its banks onto its floodplain. Trees, wetlands and open floodplains slow the water and soak it up, so the peak is lower and the flood less dangerous.

faq.q: What causes a river to flood?
faq.a: A flood happens when more water reaches a river than its channel can hold. Usually that is heavy or long-lasting rain, but melting snow, storm surges from the sea or a burst dam can do it too.
Lag time is the gap between the heaviest rain and the river's highest level. Water takes time to travel over and through the ground to reach the river.
asks: Why does a river flood after the rain stops?

faq.q: Why do towns flood more easily?
faq.a: Concrete, tarmac and roofs stop rain soaking in, and drains rush it to the river. So more water arrives faster, giving a higher peak.
asks: How do cities make flooding worse?

faq.a: A floodplain is the flat land beside a river that it covers when it floods. Floods spread fine, fertile mud there, which is why farmers have long used floodplains.
asks: Why is land near rivers fertile?

faq.a: Planting trees, restoring wetlands and letting rivers spill onto empty floodplains slow the water down. Towns also build flood walls, embankments and storage basins.

facts: The 1931 floods on China's Yangtze and Huai rivers were among the deadliest natural disasters on record.
The Nile's yearly flood spread fertile silt over Egypt's fields for thousands of years, until the Aswan High Dam was completed in 1970.

quiz.say: Why does a river in a city often flood faster than a river in a forest?
quiz.show: A city river floods faster because…

options.show: Concrete stops rain soaking in, so water rushes to the river
options.say: Concrete stops rain soaking in, so water rushes to the river

options.show: Cities get more rain than forests
options.say: Cities get more rain than forests

quiz.why: Hard surfaces and drains send rain straight to the river, shortening the lag time and raising the peak.

wrong.1: Cities do not usually get much more rain; the difference is how fast it reaches the river.
wrong.2: Trees do the opposite: they soak up rain and slow it down.
